failures.criterion: One LOADTEST_ROOT runs one step at a time (README 'Run one step': run-step.sh resets the stack before each step; 'No other heavy work on the machine during a step'). A second run-step.sh or run-series.sh on the root of a running step must be refused before it touches the stack.
failures.evidence: Started `run-step.sh conc-a --events 1 --sessions 50 --requests 10 --duration 120s`; 20 s into its window started `run-step.sh conc-b --events 1 --sessions 50 --requests 10 --duration 60s` on the same root. conc-b ran setup, start and seed, then its reset printed `stopped dispatch (pid 8325)`, `stopped listener (pid 8266)` and failed on `ERROR: database "dispatch" is being accessed by other users`, exit 1, leaving the listener stopped. conc-a then printed `run-step.sh: step conc-a done`, exit 0, with run.log showing pprof and heartbeat `connection refused` from 2 s into its window and a TABLES.md row of 0.95 offered / 0.01 committed events/s, 1.6% of requests 2xx, lock held 0%, no cpu.pprof or heap.pprof: a row that reads as a load collapse. Red test (its own commit, 'test(envoy): a second load-test run on one LOADTEST_ROOT is refused while the first holds it (red)'): packages/envoy/loadtest/run-step.test.sh; `cd packages/envoy && bash loadtest/run-step.test.sh` fails with `FAIL: a second run-step.sh on the root of a running run-step.sh was not refused: it went on to stack.sh setup (its go build ran) ...`. It fakes go and uv on PATH and holds the first run inside setup; it asserts a second run-step.sh, a run-series.sh during a run-step.sh, and a run-step.sh during a run-series.sh are each refused before their build, and that a run after the first exits is not refused. It is not yet in CI: GitHub refused the review App's push of a step for it in .github/workflows/envoy-and-contracts.yaml ('refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow ... without `workflows` permission'), so the fix adds, after the envoy job's 'Verdict test for listener-deploy-probe.sh' step: `- name: One-run-at-a-time test for loadtest/run-step.sh and run-series.sh (fakes go and uv; no stack)` / `run: bash loadtest/run-step.test.sh` / `working-directory: packages/envoy`; if the implement App cannot push a workflow either, that is the architect's to route. A scratch prototype (flock on $LOADTEST_ROOT/.run.lock in both scripts, the series exporting that it holds the lock to its own run-step.sh calls) passes all four cases; it is not committed. The repository's precedent is packages/envoy/scripts/e2e-local.sh's flock, whose comment names the trap a fix here meets: the stack's processes outlive the step, so a lock descriptor they inherit (setsid -f in stack.sh spawn) keeps the root held after the step; the next round checks on the real stack that a step after a step is not refused.

failures.criterion: A step reports the load it measured: a step whose Dispatch exits during the window must fail (non-zero exit naming the exited process), not finish as a normal row.
failures.evidence: `run-step.sh dispatch-killed --events 1 --sessions 50 --requests 10 --duration 60s`, Dispatch SIGKILLed by its stack.json pid (/legion/scratch/tmp/lt-tester/bin/envoy-dispatch) 11 s into the window: `run-step.sh: step dispatch-killed done in 130 s`, EXIT=0, TABLES.md row 0.67 offered / 0.10 committed events/s, 18.9% of requests 2xx, cpu.pprof and heap.pprof absent; run.log names only the failed pprof fetches. A Dispatch crash or OOM at a high step would read as the overload collapse the series is meant to show. No red test in the repository's suite: the package's tests run with no Postgres or NATS, and reaching this needs a live stack; the next round's real-surface check is this same command, expecting a non-zero exit that names Dispatch.

failures.criterion: README 'Requirements': 'No other heavy work on the machine during a step. meta.json records the load average before each step.' On the target pod that record must be able to show other work.
failures.evidence: On this gVisor pod /proc/loadavg read `0.00 0.00 0.00 0/0 0` 2 min into step-1x while two /proc/stat reads 5 s apart (cpu 628826 0 195805 1622367 -> 629490 0 195878 1622634) put the box at about 74% busy; every step's meta.json has loadavg_before `0.00 0.00 0.00`. Each Legion role runs in its own PID namespace, so `ps` and the sampler see none of another role's processes: this run found the implementer's whole stack still running in the pod (its ports open, its pids absent from /proc here) while meta.json said 0.00. The PR body's 'load average 0.00 before' therefore proves no idle box. A measure that works here is /proc/stat busy over a short interval before the step (the sampler already reads /proc/stat for `box busy`); the README and the PR body should name it instead.
